translationRepairs: Chen Shan of Xinxing, a petty clerk whom Jianfeng employed as his driver, had a wife famed for her beauty—and Jianfeng carried on an affair with her in secret.
Chen Shan of Xinxi, a petty clerk whom Jianfeng employed as his driver, had a wife famed for her beauty—and Jianfeng carried on an affair with her in secret.
新息 is Xinxi (county in Caizhou), not Xinxing.
Chen Shan, a minor clerk of Xinxing, served as Jianfeng's charioteer; his wife was beautiful and seductive, and [Jianfeng] took her secretly.
Chen Shan, a minor clerk of Xinxi, served as Jianfeng's charioteer; his wife was beautiful and seductive, and [Jianfeng] took her secretly.
The throne immediately appointed him acting Grand Preceptor and prefect of Tanzhou.
An edict immediately appointed Ma Yin acting Grand Preceptor and prefect of Tanzhou.
The appointee is Ma Yin, acclaimed in s0013; "him" could be misread as Zhang Ji, the subject of that sentence.
Huainan is my enemy; it certainly will not aid me.
Huainan is our enemy; it certainly will not aid us.
我/吾 here refer to Ma Yin's Hunan regime.
Guo Yu then stormed Guizhou, took the city, and proclaimed himself prefect.
Guo Yu then stormed Guizhou (歸州), took the city, and proclaimed himself prefect.
歸州 (Guizhou in Hubei) is a different place from 桂州 (Guizhou, s0023); both romanize as Guizhou.
Chuyan's wife Li told her husband, "You have heaped insults on the army, and Run has sworn to tear you apart. Better to die now than face that fate."
Chuyan's wife Li told her husband, "You have heaped insults on the army, and will be torn apart. Better to die now than face that fate."
The source (且支解) does not name Run as subject; the idiomatic version adds a name not in the text.
Dissatisfied with his lot, Xu Cun drew Run's suspicion. A spy reported that he was playing cuju, and Run said, "He is certain to rebel—he is testing how strong he still is."
Xu Cun was dissatisfied with his lot. Run sent a retainer to watch him, who found him playing cuju, and Run said, "He is certain to rebel—he is testing how strong he still is."
汭遣客伺之 (Run sent a retainer to watch him) is dropped in the translation.
In his later years he took up his father-in-law Ren Zhi, who slandered and destroyed his sons. Run killed them all with his own hand, leaving himself without heirs.
In his later years he gave office to his father-in-law, who slandered and destroyed his sons. Run killed them all with his own hand, leaving himself without heirs.
任之 means "employed him"; it is not a personal name "Ren Zhi".
In his later years he obtained his wife's father Ren Zhi, who slandered and harmed his sons; Run personally killed them all, even to the extinction of his line.
In his later years he obtained his wife's father and employed him; he slandered and harmed his sons; Run personally killed them all, even to the extinction of his line.
任之 means "employed him"; it is not a personal name.
In his later years he delighted in magicians, took their drugs, nearly died at the water's edge, and revived.
In his later years he delighted in magicians, took their drugs, came to the brink of death, and revived.
濱死 means "on the verge of death", not "at the water's edge".
Yang Xingmi dispatched Li Shenfu and Liu Cun with ten thousand men by water against Hong. Luo Yin fled Yongxing, leaving Fang Zhao and the county militia to hold the town pending further orders.
Yang Xingmi dispatched Li Shenfu and Liu Cun with ten thousand men by water against Hong. Luo Yin fled Yongxing, and the county people had Fang Zhao hold the town pending further orders.
縣民方詔守以待命: the county people had Fang Zhao hold it; 方詔 is the defender, not a companion of a militia.
The Huainan general Liu Cun dug a trench around Fu city.
The Huainan general Liu Cun dug trenches up to the city walls.
浚坎傅城 = dug trenches right up against (傅) the city; there is no "Fu city".
Bian deserters reached the Huainan camp and reported on enemy dispositions: "The Yan contingent is timid and can be taken; the Kaodao contingent is not to be faced head-on."
Bian deserters reached the Huainan camp and reported on enemy dispositions: "The Yun contingent is timid and can be taken; the Kaidao contingent is not to be faced head-on."
鄆 is Yun (Yunzhou), not Yan. 開道 is read Kāidào.
Bian deserters fled to the Huainan ramparts and reported the army's true condition, saying: "The Yan troops are cowardly and can be taken; the Kaodao troops cannot be faced.
Bian deserters fled to the Huainan ramparts and reported the army's true condition, saying: "The Yun troops are cowardly and can be taken; the Kaidao troops cannot be faced.
鄆 is Yun (Yunzhou). 開道 is read Kāidào.
He led the assault on the Kaodao contingent himself, routed it, took three hundred Bian soldiers prisoner, and paraded them beneath the walls.
He led the assault on the Kaidao contingent himself, routed it, took three hundred Bian soldiers prisoner, and paraded them beneath the walls.
He then personally attacked the Kaodao army, defeated it, captured three hundred Bian soldiers, and displayed them below the city.
He then personally attacked the Kaidao army, defeated it, captured three hundred Bian soldiers, and displayed them below the city.
Whenever he marched out to attack in battle he always prayed at Buddhist shrines, piling cakes into rhinoceroses and elephants several zhang high.
Whenever he marched out to attack in battle he always prayed at Buddhist shrines, piling cakes into rhinoceroses and elephants several xun high.
尋 is the xun (eight chi), not the zhang.

The overall commander Wang Duo sent Cui Kai to accept his surrender and secured his appointment as prefect of Suzhou. Hanhong resented the meager reward and began to speak openly of greater ambitions.

The overall commander Wang Duo sent Cui Kai to accept his surrender and secured his appointment as prefect of Suzhou (宿州). Hanhong resented the meager reward and began to speak openly of greater ambitions.
宿州 (in Anhui) is distinct from 蘇州 (s0200); both romanize as Suzhou.
Xiong made Shangyuan his western capital.
Xiong made Shangyuan his Western Prefecture (Xizhou).
西州 is a prefecture name (Western Prefecture), not a "capital".
Xiong then made Shangyuan his western prefecture.
Xiong then made Shangyuan Xizhou (the Western Prefecture).
西州 is used as a proper prefecture name.
Tian Jun met him at Yeshan and routed him utterly. Hongduo gathered his shattered remnants and prepared to flee by sea.
Tian Jun met him at Heshan and routed him utterly. Hongduo gathered his shattered remnants and prepared to flee by sea.
曷 is read hé; 曷山 is Heshan.
Jun met him in counterattack at Yeshan; Hongduo was greatly defeated, gathered his remnant troops, and wished to flee to sea.
Jun met him in counterattack at Heshan; Hongduo was greatly defeated, gathered his remnant troops, and wished to flee to sea.
曷 is read hé; 曷山 is Heshan.
Qian Liu sent his brother Qian against him. Yue had the people tattoo their foreheads in ink with the words, "We will fight the Southern Capital."
Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qian Qiu against him. Yue had the people tattoo their foreheads in ink with the words, "We will fight the Southern Capital."
The brother is 錢銶 Qian Qiu; "Qian" alone is only the shared surname.
Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qian to attack him; Yue drove the people to tattoo their foreheads in ink, saying: "We wish to fight the Southern Capital.
Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qiu to attack him; Yue drove the people to tattoo their foreheads in ink, saying: "We wish to fight the Southern Capital.
The brother is named 銶 (Qiu); Qian is only the surname.
Wang Chao, styled Xinchen, was a native of Gushi in Guangzhou.
Wang Chao, styled Xinchen, was a native of Gushi in Guangzhou (光州).
光州 must be distinguished from 廣州 (s0267), which also romanizes as Guangzhou.

Before long their force exceeded ten thousand. Xu styled himself general, retook Guangzhou, and impressed local strongmen into his ranks. Chao, formerly a county clerk, was made army steward in charge of supplies, and the troops praised his reliability.

Before long their force exceeded ten thousand. Xu styled himself general, retook Guangzhou (光州), and impressed local strongmen into his ranks. Chao, formerly a county clerk, was made army steward in charge of supplies, and the troops praised his reliability.
光州 must be distinguished from 廣州 (s0267).
Chao marched with his brothers Shenbian and Shenzhi, supporting their mother. Xu rebuked him sharply: "Armies on campaign have laws. No army is above the law."
Chao marched with his brothers Shengui and Shenzhi, supporting their mother. Xu rebuked him sharply: "Armies on campaign have laws. No army is above the law."
審邽 is read Shěnguī (邽 guī).
Chao with his younger brothers Shenbian and Shenzhi supported their mother on the march; Xu sharply reproached Chao: "I have heard that armies on campaign have laws—there is no army without law."
Chao with his younger brothers Shengui and Shenzhi supported their mother on the march; Xu sharply reproached Chao: "I have heard that armies on campaign have laws—there is no army without law."
審邽 is read Shěnguī (邽 guī).
When Chao fell ill, he entrusted military authority to Shenzhi and offered the post to Shenbian, but the offer was refused.
When Chao fell ill, he entrusted military authority to Shenzhi and Shenzhi offered to yield it to Shengui, who would not accept.
審邽 is Shengui; in 讓審邽，不許 it is Shenzhi who yields and Shengui who declines.
When Chao fell ill he had Shenzhi act as military governor by authority; he yielded to Shenbian, but this was not permitted.
When Chao fell ill he had Shenzhi act as military governor by authority; he (Shenzhi) yielded to Shengui, who did not accept.
審邽 is Shengui; the yielding party is Shenzhi.
Xingquan woke from an uneasy dream and grew restless himself. With several dozen followers he hid in the brush, ambushed Xu, bound him, and paraded him before the army.
Xingquan was startled into realizing his danger and grew uneasy himself. With several dozen followers he hid in the brush, ambushed Xu, bound him, and paraded him before the army.
怪寤 here means he was alarmed into awareness by Chao's warning, not that he woke from a dream.
Xingquan awoke from a strange dream and was also ill at ease; with several dozen close followers he hid in thick brush, ambushed and bound Xu, and displayed him to the army.
Xingquan was startled into awareness and was also ill at ease; with several dozen close followers he hid in thick brush, ambushed and bound Xu, and displayed him to the army.
怪寤 means startled into realization; no dream is mentioned.

Huang Chao's generals had meant to seize Fuzhou, but the imperial army could not take it. Chen Yan of Jian led his forces to capture the city, drove out the observation commissioner Zheng Yi, and was confirmed as prefect by edict.

Earlier, Huang Chao's generals had seized Fuzhou, and the imperial army could not retake it. Chen Yan of Jian led his forces to capture the city, drove out the observation commissioner Zheng Yi, and was confirmed as prefect by edict.
竊有 means they had usurped possession of Fuzhou, not merely intended to.

At first Huang Chao's generals meant to seize Fuzhou; the imperial army could not take it; the Jian native Chen Yan led the host to capture it, also drove out observation commissioner Zheng Yi, took the prefecture himself, and an edict at once appointed him prefect.

At first Huang Chao's generals usurped possession of Fuzhou; the imperial army could not take it; the Jian native Chen Yan led the host to capture it, also drove out observation commissioner Zheng Yi, took the prefecture himself, and an edict at once appointed him prefect.
竊有 = seized and held illegitimately.
審邽 is read Shěnguī (邽 guī).
審邽 is read Shěnguī (邽 guī).

As the Central Plains fell into chaos, many court officials fled to him for refuge. He supported them from the treasury—men such as Yang Chenxiu, Zheng Lin, Han Wo, Gui Chuanyi, Yang Zantu, and Zheng Xian owed their survival to his patronage. Shenbian had his son Yanbin establish the Hall for Recruiting Talent to receive them with full ceremony.

As the Central Plains fell into chaos, many court officials fled to him for refuge. He supported them from the treasury—men such as Yang Chengxiu, Zheng Lin, Han Wo, Gui Chuanyi, Yang Zantu, and Zheng Jian owed their survival to his patronage. Shengui had his son Yanbin establish the Hall for Recruiting Talent to receive them with full ceremony.
